issue_context.title: Remove usage of reflect.DeepEqual in framework/runtime tests
issue_context.body:
The use of `reflect.DeepEqual` makes it harder to swap implementations. We should be using `cmp` package instead, preferring `cmp.Diff` to print the differences. In the cases where this is not possible due to unexported members, we should:

1. Check if we can simply export all fields
1. If 1 is not possible and the structs are only compared in one test file, implement an explicit Comparer there, or:
1. Provide a comparer for the type.

In the case of errors, `cmpopts.EquateErrors` should be preferred.

A clear offender of this issue is `pkg/scheduler/framework/runtime/framework_test.go`. But we should fix #94695 first.

/sig scheduling
comments: /sig scheduling
/kind cleanup
I'm a new contributor and I'm interested in this issue.

Feel free to take it. You can start anywhere in `pkg/scheduler`, specially if the change doesn't depend on #94695.

Please submit small contained PRs (affecting one file and it's corresponding test if possible).
/assign HaonanFeng
/good-first-issue
/cc
Sorry, I was business trip for the last few days and I'm working on this.

> * If 1 is not possible and the structs are only compared in one test file, implement an explicit Comparer there, or:

We can use `cmp.AllowUnexported()` as an option:

```go
if diff := cmp.Diff(gotStatus, tt.wantStatus, cmp.AllowUnexported(framework.Status{})); diff != "" {
```

-1 on `AllowUnexported`

I think we should define clear semantics of when 2 statuses are equal. Otherwise we are not wining anything from moving off `reflect.Equal`

> I think we should define clear semantics of when 2 statuses are equal.

If the comparison semantics is not ambiguous, why don't we use `AllowUnexported` directly? Take the `framework.Status` for example, it's clear that we're going to compare all (private) fields (reason, code, etc.).

It is actually a bit ambiguous.

Say a plugin returns `{Unschedulable, "not enough CPU"}`. Then we annotate that as coming from the FitPlugin in runtime.go:
So `{Unschedulable, "FitPlugin failed: not enough CPU"}`. Now they are different, but they shouldn't be.

Arguably, we are wrapping statuses the wrong way. That's precisely what https://blog.golang.org/go1.13-errors is trying to solve. However, we are not talking about errors here.

/unassign @HaonanFeng
Sorry, we need more deliberation here.

That said, I don't think we do decision making with "reasons", only with "errors". So we don't need to redefine the Status struct.

But we should fix how we compare errors. I think a proper comparison, at least for now would be:
code is equal, reasons are equal, errors compare the same with `errors.Is`
alternatively, we expose all the attributes and just use `cmpopt.EquateErrors`.

`cmpopt.EquateErrors` sounds good to me as well, I don't have a strong option.

BTW: if we go with the customized `ComparerFn`, it seems we should make the error comparison symmetric:

```
errors.Is(x.err, y.err) || errors.Is(y.err, x.err)
```

Ref: 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/0dd6bf625814ab6ef9f93fbee40cde6d6206d932/vendor/github.com/google/go-cmp/cmp/cmpopts/equate.go#L155
Kind of. Export the Status fields (make the first letter uppercase) instead of using `cmp.Exporter`

> Then in `Diff`, `cmp.Exporter` judge whether it is "Status", if it is, then return the field of status:

I don't think we'd like to do that way. Just simply make the private fields of Status to public, and use `cmpopts.EquateErrors()`.
